cards.title: Introduction to Python Packaging
cards.content:
Packaging is the process of organizing your Flask application into a standard format that can be easily installed, shared, and deployed. It transforms your project from a mere collection of scripts into a distributable library or application.

Key benefits include dependency management, versioning, and seamless distribution via PyPI or private repositories.

cards.title: The pyproject.toml File
cards.content:
Modern Python packaging relies on pyproject.toml, as defined by PEP 518 and PEP 621. This file specifies build system requirements and project metadata.

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "my_flask_app"
version = "0.1.0"
dependencies = [
    "Flask>=3.0.0",
    "SQLAlchemy>=2.0.0"
]

cards.title: Flask Application Layout
cards.content:
A standard packagable Flask application uses the application factory pattern and a structured layout:

my_flask_app/
├── pyproject.toml
├── README.md
└── src/
    └── myapp/
        ├── __init__.py
        ├── models.py
        └── views.py

Using the src/ layout prevents accidental imports of local code without installing the package first.

content.instructions: Order the steps required to package and upload a Flask application.

steps.text: Create pyproject.toml with project metadata and dependencies
Install build tools: pip install build twine
Generate distribution archives using python -m build
Upload the package to PyPI using twine upload dist/*

cards.title: Managing Dependencies
cards.content:
In your pyproject.toml, dependencies are declared under the [project] table. For development dependencies (like testing or linting tools), use optional dependencies or dependency groups.

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=7.0.0",
    "flake8>=6.0.0"
]

cards.title: Virtual Environments and Editable Installs
cards.content:
When developing your packaged Flask app, use an editable install so changes in your source code are immediately reflected in your environment without reinstalling.

pip install -e .

This links the package in the current directory to your active virtual environment.

cards.title: Conclusion and Best Practices
cards.content:
You have learned how to package a Flask application using standard tools like pyproject.toml, structuring your app with an src/ layout, declaring dependencies, and using editable installs for efficient development.

Always test your package installation in a clean virtual environment before publishing!
